## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [31. Juli 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.151
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.151
- Datum: 31.7.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
c/o Viking Press 18 East 48 Street
July 31st, 41
Dear Hannah & Manfred, many thanks for your letter. Eva is just
here for a visit and I hope to induce her to write some lines - no,
she really likes now to write and is a big and intelligent girl.
Now about us. We had finally - after more than a year - a little
house with a maid for four weeks and this and on the other
hand my deep depression did let me work like seven devils, I
have finished in this month my autobiography, written it with
my own hand so quickly that Lotte could not yet follow. Now I will
leave the manuscript for two months and we shall see later if
I will have to change. In any case I have no hurry to publish
it, I wanted only to have it ready. It goes till to the first
day of the second world-war. We shall let send you a copy
of the the Brail book when it comes out in September. The
small book on Vespucci will appear much later. As to Hilmot
please tell him that your task was only meant to be a temporary
one; if new ~~difficult~~ questions arise we shall deal with them
ourselves. The idea that you should have to go to London and
loose your time is oppressive to me; I know how much you
have to do and that physical and psychic rest is necessary for
you. So never worry about our worries we want to take care
of ourselves. When does Manfred start his practice as Xray
specialist?
About our travelling plans you will have our news soon. We
are ready to start in August because we have to be there in
the lecturing season but there you can never tell till to the
last moment in such times if there are no changes. We would
do our best of course to come back here after some time
- what I want, badly want is some rest and New York is not
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig. Tinte auf Papier.
Rückseite des ersten Blattes, durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite sichtbar. Leer.

pages.transcription:
the right place for it. I have worked hard and want a little
dolce far niente. If you would have been with us in all these
months you would understand this much better - this wandering
this eternal indecision for the next few months was exhausting.
Now I would like to give these {indeed} times to our friend
Kormendi. I got his book and want to thank him. To Rose
Mann please say that I am not more interested in books in
the next time, as I have no opportunity to read books and to
admire drawings; perhaps later again! I like to avoid all
which complicates - I have but one wish to sit quietly and
to write my own books, to know you without worries and not
connected with my own, to see your child growing up and
in excellent hands, to dream from peace and to give Lotte a
happier life than she has with her old and depressive husband
You will hear from us soon. Enjoy the summer as much as
you can with Manfred and all your friends and your sister.
Yours truly

Stefan Zweig

Dearest Mummy,
I am here with Auntie and
Uncle. I am leaving this afternoon. Yester-
day aunt Elizabeth came with Nancy.
I am invited to them for a few days.
Does Ursel have scarlet fever?
I hope not. How is the house and
the garden? The Millers, the Robins, and
so on. Give my regards to everyone,
Many, many kisses
Eva
pages.notes: Zweite Seite des Briefes, gefolgt von einem kurzen Brief von Eva an ihre Mutter. Handschriftlich.
Rückseite des zweiten Blattes, durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite sichtbar. Leer.
